author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The cost of moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz has climbed into a range of $10 million to $20 million for some voyages after the Iran war, an Emirates National Oil Company executive said Wednesday.

ENOC director Paul Bradshaw told the APPEC conference that cargo insurance could reach 5% to 6% of a shipment’s value, potentially adding about $10 million. Additional war-risk premiums that were previously zero can now run as high as 10%, Reuters reported.

Bradshaw said some market participants were choosing to go without insurance, while a limited number of shipowners were willing to accept the safety risk. Some national oil companies have taken greater control of their own shipping operations.

The figures are an industry executive’s reported estimates, not a universal tariff for every vessel. Actual costs vary by cargo, route, insurer and risk assessment. Even so, the increase shows how conflict can affect energy markets without an immediate change in production: higher insurance, longer routes and fewer willing ships can tighten vessel availability and raise delivered costs.
dek: An ENOC executive said insurance and war-risk premiums can push some voyage costs into an eight-figure range through the key oil route.
headline: Hormuz oil-transit costs surge as insurers price war risk
